Protocol > Part Reference > WirePart Details and Examples

#### `handoff` *(Reserved)*
Emitted during human escalation:

```json
{
  "type": "handoff",
  "status": "queued",
  "pollAfterMs": 3000
}
```

`status` values: `'requested'`, `'queued'`, `'connected'`, or `'ended'`.

#### `agent-message` *(Reserved)*
Message sent by a human support agent:

```json
{
  "type": "agent-message",
  "messageId": "msg_agent_01",
  "text": "Hello, I am joining to help answer your question.",
  "agent": { "name": "Sarah", "avatarUrl": "https://example.com/avatars/sarah.png" },
  "timestamp": 1792411200000
}
```

#### `suggestions` *(Reserved)*
Suggested replies for the user:

```json
{
  "type": "suggestions",
  "items": ["What are your pricing plans?", "Contact sales", "View API docs"]
}
```

#### `error`
Reports an error that occurs after streaming has begun (see [Errors During Streaming](#errors-during-streaming)):

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "code": "provider_error",
  "retryable": true,
  "message": "The AI provider failed to complete the turn."
}
```

#### `finish`
Sent immediately before `data: [DONE]`. Closes the turn:

```json
{
  "type": "finish",
  "reason": "stop",
  "usage": {
    "inputTokens": 142,
    "outputTokens": 38
  }
}
```

- `reason` enum values (`WireFinishReason`):
  - **Currently emitted by the server**:
    - `'stop'`: The model finished generating naturally.
    - `'length'`: Generation was cut off by token limits (`maxTokens`).
    - `'error'`: Turn ended due to an error.
    - `'aborted'`: Request was aborted by the client or connection termination.
  - **Reserved for future releases (not currently emitted)**:
    - `'client-tool-calls'`
    - `'approval-required'`
    - `'handoff'`
- `usage`: Only included when `exposeUsage: true` is configured on the server handler (omitted by default for privacy).

---

chunks.text:
Upgrading to 1.0 > `@chatcops/core` > `AIProvider` has `chat?()`, and no `chatSync()`

A custom provider needs `step()` or `chat()`. Nothing ever called `chatSync()`, so delete it from yours. Code that typed a variable as `AIProvider` and called `.chat()` on it has to check for it first, since a provider may have only `step()`.

AI Providers > Options > Temperature on newer models

Claude's API no longer takes `temperature` on any model (API version 2026-10-21), and OpenAI reasoning models (GPT-5 and later, o-series) don't accept a custom one either. ChatCops leaves it out for those and logs a one-time warning. Use `effort` instead. Gemini and other OpenAI models still use it.

Security > What each layer stops

| Layer | Option | Stops | Doesn't stop |
|---|---|---|---|
| Allowed origins | `allowedOrigins` | Other sites putting your bot on their pages | Scripts, which can send any `Origin` |
| Session tokens | `sessionSecrets` | Reading or continuing someone else's conversation with a leaked or guessed id | A script that asks for its own sessions |
| Turnstile | `turnstile` | Cheap scripted session minting | Paid solver farms |
| Rate limits | `rateLimit` (on by default) | One IP sending requests faster than a person types | Many IPs |
| Budgets | `budgets` (on by default) | Any one conversation, IP or day costing more than you set | Nothing. This is the backstop. |

No single layer is enough on its own. Allowed origins and sessions stop the easy cases. Budgets put a ceiling on the bill whatever gets through, and `budgets.globalPerDay` is the one number that caps it all. There's no default for it, because no single number fits every site, so set one.

Rate limits and budgets are counted in `storage`. With the default memory storage, each serverless instance counts on its own, and a limit of 30 a minute becomes 30 per instance. Use a [store package](/server/storage/) in production.

Vercel Edge Full Example > Environment Variables

Set in Vercel dashboard → Settings → Environment Variables:

```bash
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
CHATCOPS_SESSION_SECRET=...   # openssl rand -base64 32
WEBHOOK_URL=https://hooks.zapier.com/...
```

Storage > Custom stores

The history sent to the model is trimmed to about 32,000 tokens: the visitor's first message plus as many recent ones as fit. Stored history keeps up to 100 messages per conversation.

The complete interface is defined by [`ConversationStore`](https://github.com/codercops/chatcops/blob/dev/packages/core/src/storage/types.ts). The broader `ChatCopsStorage` object can also provide optional counter, KV, and event stores for distributed rate limits, turn locks, and analytics.

Vercel Edge Full Example

A production-ready Vercel Edge Function with lead capture, knowledge base, and analytics.

Upgrading from 0.5 > Upgrade the server first

Upgrade the server, deploy it, then update the widget. A widget from 0.5 or earlier sends requests without `"protocol": 1`, and the new server answers those in the exact 0.5 format until 1.0. The server logs one line the first time it does, so you can tell when old widgets are still around (cached pages, a pinned CDN version).

The 0.6 widget also works against a 0.5 server, so the order isn't critical. It just gets more from a 0.6 one: reply ids that regenerate can name, and a clear "cut off" state when a stream ends early.

Theming > AI-generated replies

Replies written by the model carry `data-ai-generated="true"`. User messages and the welcome message don't. The messages are inside the widget's shadow root, so the page's CSS can't select them, but scripts can:

```js
document.getElementById('chatcops-root').shadowRoot.querySelectorAll('[data-ai-generated]');
```

Storage > Vector stores > Cloudflare Vectorize

`@chatcops/store-cloudflare` can add semantic and keyword retrieval with a D1 database and a Cloudflare Vectorize index:

```bash
npm install @chatcops/store-cloudflare
```

Create the Vectorize index with the same dimensions as your embedding model and cosine distance, then create metadata indexes for every key used in filters:

```bash
npx wrangler vectorize create-index CHATCOPS_VECTORS --dimensions=1024 --metric=cosine
npx wrangler vectorize create-metadata-index CHATCOPS_VECTORS --property-name=locale --type=string
npx wrangler vectorize create-metadata-index CHATCOPS_VECTORS --property-name=collection --type=string
```

Bind both services and pass the same dimension count to the store:

```typescript
import { cloudflareStorage, type CloudflareBindings } from '@chatcops/store-cloudflare';

declare const env: CloudflareBindings;

const storage = cloudflareStorage({
  d1: env.DB,
  vectorize: env.CHATCOPS_VECTORS,
  vectorDimensions: 1024,
});
```

Vectorize stores embeddings and filterable metadata; D1 keeps the full text and source details and provides FTS5 keyword search. Create a metadata index for each key you pass in `filter`; unindexed metadata cannot be filtered by Vectorize. The index metric must be `cosine`. Vectorize writes can take a few seconds to become searchable.

AI Providers > Conversation history

Before each request ChatCops cleans up the stored history so every provider accepts it. The history always starts with a user message, and two messages in a row from the same side are joined into one. This happens, for example, when a reply failed and the visitor sent their message again.

These start from the same options. Swap the storage for the one you use.

Testing your bot > Eval files

`defaults` at the top of the file applies to every test in it. A test's own values win, and tool mocks are merged:

```yaml
version: 1
name: Orders
defaults:
  pageContext: { url: "https://acme.com/account", title: "Your account" }
  mocks:
    tools:
      lookup_order: { success: true, data: { status: "shipped" } }
tests:
  - name: says where the order is
    repeat: 5
    passRate: 0.8
    turns:
      - user: Where is order A-1001?
        expect:
          - calls-tool: lookup_order
          - calls-tool: { name: lookup_order, args: { id: "A-1001" } }
          - no-tool-call: cancel_order
          - contains: shipped
```

A mock for a tool your config doesn't have is an error, so a renamed tool can't leave a mock behind that no longer does anything.

Eval files can also be modules (`.chat.ts`, `.chat.mjs`) that export the same object as their default, when you'd rather build tests in code.

Testing your bot > Recorded replays

Running tests calls your model for real, which costs tokens and needs the API key. For CI, record the calls once and replay them:

```bash
npx chatcops test --record   # calls the APIs and saves what they answer
npx chatcops test --replay   # answers every call from the recordings
```

`--record` saves each eval file's calls next to it, in `__cassettes__/<file>.jsonl` (so `evals/pricing.chat.yaml` records to `evals/__cassettes__/pricing.chat.jsonl`). It records every HTTP call a test makes: the model, embedding calls for knowledge search, and tools that call APIs without a mock. Commit the folder with your eval files.

When the `CI` environment variable is set, as it is on GitHub Actions and most CI services, `chatcops test` replays by default, so CI needs no API keys and costs nothing. A provider config without an `apiKey` gets a stand-in key during replay, since nothing is sent. Keep the config file loading when a key is missing: read `process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` as it is, and don't throw at load time. `--live` calls the APIs anyway.

Each call is matched by its method, URL and body within its test. Any change that changes what gets sent fails the test instead of passing on an old answer:

- a new word in the system prompt
- another model
- a tool added or removed
- a new knowledge page in the context

The message says where the request changed:

```text
✗ evals/pricing.chat.yaml > quotes the Team price
    A call changed since it was recorded (POST https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages, at system[0].text). Run chatcops test --record to record it again.
```

Run `--record` again after a change like that, check that the tests still pass, and commit the new recordings. `--record --filter` updates only the tests it ran, and recordings of tests you deleted are dropped the next time the file is recorded.

A few things to know about recordings:

A second message sent while a reply for the same conversation is still streaming is refused (`409 conversation_busy` in protocol v1, `provider_error` for 0.5 widgets). The widget doesn't let visitors do this, so it only shows up with custom clients that send in parallel.

chunks.text:
Upgrading from 0.5 > Worth turning on

None of these are on by default. Each one closes a gap that 0.5 had no answer for.

- `storage`: conversations, limits and the one-reply lock shared by every server instance. On serverless, memory doesn't last between requests, and the server warns about it. See [Storage](/server/storage/).
- `allowedOrigins`: only your sites can put the chat on their pages. See [Allowed origins](/server/setup/#allowed-origins).
- `sessionSecrets`, and optionally `turnstile`: a guessed or leaked conversation id is useless, and a script has to pass Turnstile to start a session. Start with `requireSession: false` (`allowAnonymous: true` from 1.0) while 0.5 widgets are still cached, since they don't send tokens. See [Session tokens](/server/setup/#session-tokens).
- `budgets.globalPerDay`: a daily cap on total spend, in tokens or dollars. There's no default.
- Tools with `inputSchema`: a full JSON Schema, nested objects and arrays included, instead of the flat `parameters` form. See [Tools](/core/tools/).

For custom clients, the new response format is [protocol v1](/server/setup/#protocol-v1), with typed parts and real HTTP statuses. Apps built on the AI SDK's `useChat` can use [`chatcopsAiSdkHandler`](/server/ai-sdk/).

ChatCops Documentation > Architecture

```
┌──────────────────┐         ┌──────────────────┐
│   Your Website   │  SSE    │   Your Server    │
│                  │ ──────► │                  │
│  <script> tag    │ ◄────── │  @chatcops/server│
│  @chatcops/widget│ stream  │  ├─ Provider     │
│  Shadow DOM      │         │  ├─ Knowledge    │
│  Chat Panel      │         │  ├─ Tools        │
└──────────────────┘         │  └─ Analytics    │
                             └──────────────────┘
```

Protocol > Part Reference

There are 13 variants defined in `WirePart`. Ten are actively emitted by `@chatcops/server` today, while three are reserved for specialized features or future capabilities:

| Part Type | Purpose | Fields | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | First event of every reply. Identifies the turn and conversation. | `protocol: 1`, `conversationId: string`, `messageId: string`, `resumed?: boolean`, `capabilities?: { session?: boolean }` | **Emitted** |
| `text-start` | Marks the beginning of an assistant text block. | `id: string` | **Emitted** |
| `text-delta` | Streams a chunk of text content for a text block. | `id: string`, `delta: string` | **Emitted** |
| `text-end` | Marks the end of an assistant text block. | `id: string` | **Emitted** |
| `source` | Citations or document references used by knowledge base / RAG. | `sourceId: string`, `url: string`, `title?: string`, `snippet?: string` | **Emitted** |
| `tool-call` | Signals that a tool invocation has started. | `toolCallId: string`, `toolName: string`, `input: unknown`, `executor: 'server' \| 'client' \| 'mcp'`, `needsApproval?: boolean`, `title?: string` | **Emitted** |
| `tool-result` | Emits the execution outcome of a tool call. | `toolCallId: string`, `output?: unknown`, `error?: string` | **Emitted** |
| `lead-captured` | Emitted when the built-in lead capture tool successfully gathers visitor information. | `lead: Record<string, unknown>` | **Emitted** |
| `handoff` | Human agent handoff status changes. | `status: 'requested' \| 'queued' \| 'connected' \| 'ended'`, `agent?: WireAgent`, `pollAfterMs?: number` | *Reserved* |
| `agent-message` | Direct message from a live human agent. | `messageId: string`, `text: string`, `agent: WireAgent`, `timestamp: number` | *Reserved* |
| `suggestions` | List of clickable quick-reply prompt options. | `items: string[]` | *Reserved* |
| `error` | In-stream failure notification (e.g., provider error or budget exceeded). | `code: WireErrorCode`, `retryable: boolean`, `message?: string`, `retryAfterMs?: number`, `scope?: 'conversation' \| 'session' \| 'ip' \| 'global'` | **Emitted** |
| `finish` | Final protocol event of every assistant turn. | `reason: WireFinishReason`, `usage?: { inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number }`, `pendingToolCalls?: string[]`, `resumeToken?: string` | **Emitted** |

Cloudflare Worker Full Example > Without a Durable Object

Leave out `counters` and the `COUNTERS` binding, and the counters go to D1 as well. Limits still hold across isolates, since each count is one atomic D1 statement, but every count is a D1 write. Turn locks always live in D1.

Knowledge Base > FAQ Knowledge Source > How FAQ Matching Works

1. User's query is tokenized into words
2. Each FAQ pair is scored by word frequency overlap (question + answer)
3. Top 5 matching FAQs are returned as context
4. Context is formatted as `Q: ...\nA: ...` and injected into the AI prompt

Rate limits and the per-IP budget key on the visitor's IP. The server now reads it only from headers the platform sets itself. On Vercel and Cloudflare that just works. Express uses `req.ip`, which follows `app.set('trust proxy', ...)`. Anywhere else (Netlify, a Node server behind your own proxy, Bun, Deno), set `clientIp` to read your host's header. Until you do, per-IP limits are skipped, with one warning. The server used to trust the first `X-Forwarded-For` entry, which a visitor can set to anything. chunks.text:
Testing your bot > Judged by a model

Some things a reply should do don't fit in a `contains`: "confirms the demo without inventing a meeting time", "apologizes once and doesn't argue". A `judge` assertion has a second model grade the reply against a rubric:

```yaml
expect:
  - judge: "Confirms the demo request without inventing a meeting time."
  - judge: { rubric: "Apologizes once and doesn't argue.", threshold: 0.8 }
```

The judge sees the rubric and the conversation so far, scores the last reply from 0 to 1, and gives a reason. The assertion passes at `threshold` or above (0.7 when you don't set one), and a failure prints the score and the reason.

By default the judge is the cheap model of a different provider than your bot's: Gemini's default model, or OpenAI's when the bot runs on Gemini. A model grading its own answers tends to score them too kindly. Its key comes from `GEMINI_API_KEY` (or `GOOGLE_API_KEY`), `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, and without one the run stops before it starts instead of skipping the judged tests. Every run prints which judge it used. To choose it yourself, pass `--judge-model openai:gpt-5-mini`, or set `judge` in the config:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from '@chatcops/cli';

export default defineConfig({
  server: { provider: { type: 'claude', apiKey: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY! }, systemPrompt: 'You answer questions about Acme.' },
  judge: { type: 'openai', apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY!, model: 'gpt-5-mini' },
});
```

A judge's scores can change when its model changes, so keep the same judge for a suite, and re-record when you switch. Judge calls are recorded and replayed like the bot's, so in CI the same verdicts come back without a key.

API Reference > Methods > `ChatCops.close()`

Close the chat panel.

- **Popup mode:** Hides the panel and resets the FAB icon.
- **Inline mode:** Hides the panel. Call `open()` to show it again.

```typescript
ChatCops.close();
```

Server Setup > Session tokens

With Express, mount the middleware with `app.use('/api/chat', ...)` so `/api/chat/session` reaches it. On Vercel or Next.js, export the same handler from a second route file at `app/api/chat/session/route.ts`. A Cloudflare Worker gets every path already.

Chat requests without a token get `401 session_required`, an expired token gets `401 token_expired`, and a token for another conversation gets `401 conversation_mismatch`.

A server without `sessionSecrets` refuses to start unless it sets `allowAnonymous: true`, which accepts chat without tokens. Set it with `sessionSecrets` too while widgets before 0.6, which don't send tokens, are still around: requests without a token then go through, and the ones that send one are still checked. Set it alone for a server only you reach, such as a local test, or one behind your own login. Clients that don't fetch tokens, such as the AI SDK's `useChat`, need it as well (see [AI SDK](/server/ai-sdk/)). The short examples on other pages leave `sessionSecrets` out to keep to their point. Add it to yours.

To change the secret, put the new one first and keep the old one until its tokens have expired: `sessionSecrets: [newSecret, oldSecret]`. New tokens are signed with the first, and any of them verifies.

ChatCopsBot > Blocking it

Add a group to your `robots.txt`:

```
User-agent: ChatCopsBot
Disallow: /
```

Or allow only part of the site:

```
User-agent: ChatCopsBot
Allow: /docs/
Disallow: /
```

Whoever runs the crawler can turn the `robots.txt` check off or change the user agent, the same as with any crawler library. If one is ignoring your `robots.txt`, block it by IP the way you would any other client. If you think this software is being misused, [open an issue](https://github.com/codercops/chatcops/issues).

Testing your bot > Eval files

By default the command runs every `evals/**/*.chat.yaml` file. Pass globs to pick others:

```bash
npx chatcops test "evals/pricing/*.chat.yaml"
```

An eval file has a name and a list of tests. Each test is one conversation, a turn at a time:

```yaml
version: 1
name: Pricing
tests:
  - name: quotes the Team price
    tags: [pricing]
    turns:
      - user: How much is the Team plan?
        expect:
          - contains: "$19"
          - not-contains: "$29"

  - name: remembers the plan on a follow-up
    turns:
      - user: Tell me about the Team plan.
      - user: How much is it per year?
        expect:
          - contains: "$190"
```

Each assertion has one key. `contains` takes a string or a list of strings that must all appear in the reply, `judge` has a model grade the reply ([below](#judged-by-a-model)), and every assertion also works with a `not-` prefix to say the opposite. An assertion name that doesn't exist fails the whole run before anything is sent, so a typo can't make a test pass by checking nothing.

Three assertions catch a prompt change that makes replies longer, slower or more expensive:

- `tokens-under: 800` checks the turn's input plus output tokens. `tokens-under: { input: 600, output: 200 }` checks them separately, and you can give only one of them. A turn without usage fails.
- `latency-under: 3000` checks the time to the end of the reply, in milliseconds. Replays answer at once, so it only means something in live and recorded runs.
- `cost-under: 0.01` checks what the turn cost in US dollars. It needs the model in `prices` ([Costs](#costs)), and a turn without a price fails with a reason that says so.

Two assertions check what ChatCops adds to a reply:

chunks.text:
Server Setup > Budgets

Budgets cap what replies can cost, so a script hammering your endpoint can't run up the bill. They're counted in `storage`, so they hold across instances.

They're on by default:

| Scope | Default | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `perConversation` | 200 replies | The widget keeps a conversation across visits, so this counts replies rather than tokens, which would grow with the size of your system prompt. |
| `perIpPerDay` | 2M tokens | The cost backstop. A script can start new conversations at will, but not new IPs as easily. |
| `globalPerDay` | none | No single number fits every site. Set one. |

The server logs the budgets in force once at startup:

```
[chatcops] Budgets: 200 replies per conversation (default), 2M tokens per IP per day (default). No daily total is set; `budgets.globalPerDay` caps your whole bill. Set `budgets` to change them, or `budgets: false` to turn them off.
```

A scope you set replaces its default whole. `false` turns a scope off, and `budgets: false` turns them all off:

```typescript
import type { ChatCopsServerConfig } from '@chatcops/server';

const config: Partial<ChatCopsServerConfig> = {
  budgets: {
    perConversation: { tokens: 400_000 },            // over the conversation's lifetime
    perIpPerDay: { tokens: 2_000_000, messages: 200 },
    globalPerDay: { usd: 20 },                        // the backstop
    // What a request cost, for the dollar cap. Price cached input at its discount.
    price: (usage: { inputTokens: number; outputTokens: number }) => (usage.inputTokens * 1 + usage.outputTokens * 5) / 1_000_000,
  },
};
```

Protocol > Request Body > Common Request Fields

| Field | Type | Required? | Constraints & Behavior | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `protocol` | `number` | Optional | Set to `1` to request protocol v1 streaming. Evaluated as `protocol >= 1`. | `1` |
| `conversationId` | `string` | **Yes** | 1–128 characters. Identifies the conversation thread across turns. | `"c_8f2a1b9c"` |
| `message` | `string` | **Yes** | 1–10,000 characters. The user message text. | `"Hello, what plans do you offer?"` |
| `messageId` | `string` | Optional | 1–128 characters. Client-assigned ID for the user message. Used for idempotency: re-sending an already answered `messageId` replays the saved assistant reply without invoking the AI model again. | `"msg_usr_101"` |
| `regenerate` | `boolean` \| `object` | Optional | `true` replaces the latest assistant reply (or the reply corresponding to `messageId`). `{ assistantMessageId: string }` (1–128 chars) targets a specific assistant message for regeneration. | `{ "assistantMessageId": "msg_ast_202" }` |
| `pageContext` | `object` | Optional | Information about the page where the client is active. Evaluated and placed in system context. | See [Nested Structures](#nested-request-structures) |
| `locale` | `string` | Optional | Max 10 characters. Client browser or device locale (e.g., `"en-US"`, `"es"`). Prompts the model to reply in that language. | `"en-US"` |
| `userData` | `Record<string, string>` | Optional | Pre-chat form or visitor metadata. Max 50 keys; each key max 100 characters; each value max 500 characters. Locked from the first message in storage. | `{ "plan": "pro", "company": "Acme" }` |

:::note
The TypeScript interface `ChatRequestV1` in `@chatcops/core/protocol` contains additional fields reserved for a future release (such as `toolResults`, `toolApprovals`, `clientTools`, and `resumeToken`), which the current server ignores.
:::

Vercel Adapter > Environment Variables

Set these in your Vercel dashboard or `.env.local`:

```bash
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
# or
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...
# or
GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY=...

# Signs session tokens: openssl rand -base64 32
CHATCOPS_SESSION_SECRET=...
```

Storage

The server uses storage for conversation history and, when the configured store provides the capability, counters, turn locks, and analytics events.

By default, conversations are kept in memory for one server process. The memory store holds up to 1000 conversations, evicting the least recently used first, and drops conversations that have been idle for 7 days. That is useful for local development, but it is not reliable for Vercel, Lambda, Workers, or any multi-instance deployment: instances do not share memory, and a restart removes the data. Use a persistent store when conversations must survive restarts or be available to every instance.

To change the memory store's limits, pass your own as `storage`:

```typescript
import { memoryStorage } from '@chatcops/core';

const storage = memoryStorage({
  maxConversations: 5000,                  // default 1000, least recently used dropped first
  conversationTtlMs: 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000,  // default 7 days idle
  maxKeys: 50_000,                          // counters and keys each, default 10,000
  maxEvents: 50_000,                        // analytics events, default 10,000, oldest dropped first
});
```

Past `maxKeys`, expired counters and keys are swept first, and only then are the oldest dropped.

Storage > Retention > Cloudflare Workers

Register the cron trigger in `wrangler.toml`:

```toml
name = "chatcops-worker"
main = "src/index.ts"
compatibility_date = "2024-01-01"

[triggers]
crons = ["0 3 * * *"]
```

When using a custom conversation store, the store must implement `ConversationStore.purge` for scheduled cleanup to work. `purge()` returns `null` when the store does not implement it, making scheduled cleanup a no-op.

:::note
The in-memory store implements `purge()`, but each process or Worker instance only purges its own in-memory data. Scheduled cleanup is most useful when the application uses shared, persistent storage.
:::

Knowledge Base > Retrieval from a vector store

Use [Cohere](https://docs.cohere.com/reference/rerank) or [Voyage](https://docs.voyageai.com/reference/reranker-api) to improve the ordering of retrieved candidates. `cohereReranker` defaults to `rerank-v5.0-pro`, while `voyageReranker` defaults to `rerank-3`. Both use the same reranker interface, so either can be passed to `hybridRetriever` in the same way:

```typescript
import { cohereReranker, hybridRetriever, memoryVectors, openaiEmbedder } from '@chatcops/core';

const embedder = openaiEmbedder({ apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY! });
const vectors = memoryVectors({ dimensions: embedder.dimensions });
const reranker = cohereReranker({ apiKey: process.env.COHERE_API_KEY! });

const retriever = hybridRetriever({ store: vectors, embedder, reranker });
```

Each embedder and reranker that calls an API takes `baseUrl`, for a proxy in front of it. For `openaiEmbedder` it can be any OpenAI-compatible embeddings API, such as a local model server. The default is the provider's own API.

`workersAiReranker({ ai })` uses Cloudflare's [`@cf/baai/bge-reranker-base`](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/models/bge-reranker-base/) model through the Workers AI binding. It sends the query and candidate text to the model, then maps its ranked context ids back to the original chunks. It uses the same `env.AI` binding as `workersAiEmbedder`; add this binding to `wrangler.toml` if you have not already:

```toml
[ai]
binding = "AI"
```

`memoryVectors` keeps the whole index in memory, which suits tests and small sites. It holds at most `maxRecords` chunks (50,000 by default), and an upsert past that fails rather than dropping anything. For a bigger index, or one that survives a restart, use one of the [vector stores](/server/storage/#vector-stores).

The index has to be built and searched with the same embedder; a retriever refuses an embedder whose vectors are a different size from the store's. A command that builds the index from your sitemap is next.

API Reference > Methods > `ChatCops.setContext(data)`

Details the bot should know for the next messages, such as the visitor's plan or what's in their cart. They're sent with each message as page context: at most 20 fields, keys up to 40 characters, values up to 500. The bot sees them as details the page added, not as verified facts. `setContext(null)` removes them. Nothing is sent when `pageContext: false`.

```typescript
ChatCops.setContext({ plan: 'Team', seats: '12' });
```

Knowledge Base > Building an index from your site > Ingest options

`sources` is a list of any of these:

| Source | Reads |
|---|---|
| `{ type: 'sitemap', url }` | A sitemap, a sitemap index, or a gzipped one (`.xml.gz`) |
| `{ type: 'urls', urls }` | The pages you list |
| `{ type: 'directory', path, baseUrl }` | Local `.md`, `.mdx` and `.html` files, cited as if published under `baseUrl` |

The rest of the config:

Widget Configuration > Programmatic Configuration > Streaming inactivity timeout

Set `timeout` in `ChatCops.init()` to change the inactivity timeout in milliseconds.
The default is `30000` (30 seconds). It starts when a request begins and restarts
whenever a nonempty stream chunk arrives, including heartbeat comments, partial
SSE events and malformed data. It measures received transport activity, not the
time between displayed text updates or the total response duration.

A response can stream for longer than the timeout as long as chunks keep arriving.
A request that never responds, or a stream that stops sending data, fails with a
timeout error. Use a larger value for backends with longer silent periods. This
option is available through programmatic configuration.

Server Setup > Response format

The server answers in one of two formats. The widget from 0.6 on sends `"protocol": 1` in the request body and gets protocol v1. Requests without it, from widgets before 0.6 or older custom clients, get the 0.5 format, which keeps working until 1.0. A client can also ask for v1 with an `x-chatcops-protocol: 1` header. The server logs one line the first time it answers in the 0.5 format, so you can tell when old widgets are still around. `chatcopsAiSdkHandler` answers in a third format, the AI SDK's, for apps built on `useChat` (see [AI SDK](/server/ai-sdk/)).

The server writes one reply per conversation at a time, so a second message sent while a reply is streaming is refused instead of answering the same history twice. The widget doesn't let visitors send while a reply streams, so this only shows up with custom clients.

Each reply is saved as one assistant message with its parts: the text, and every tool call and result in order. It's saved after each tool round, so a reply cut off partway still has the finished tool steps. A retry of a message that already has a finished reply gets that reply again, without calling the model.

Quick Start > 3. Test It

1. Start your server: `node server.js`
2. Open your HTML page in a browser
3. Click the chat bubble — you're live!

Server Setup

The `@chatcops/server` package provides a universal chat handler that works with any HTTP framework via adapters.

API Reference > Methods > `ChatCops.clear()`

Like `newConversation()`, and also removes what the widget saved in this browser: the transcript and the pre-chat answers, so the form shows again. Use it when a visitor signs out.

```typescript
ChatCops.clear();
```

API Reference > Methods > `ChatCops.toggle()`

Open the chat if it's closed, and close it if it's open. With the script tag build, the first call loads the chat.

```typescript
document.querySelector('#help-btn')?.addEventListener('click', () => ChatCops.toggle());
```

Cloudflare Workers Adapter > Widget Configuration

```html
<script
  src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@chatcops/widget/dist/chatcops.min.js"
  data-api-url="https://chatcops.your-domain.workers.dev"
></script>
```

Widget Configuration > WidgetConfig Interface

See the [pre-chat form guide](/widget/pre-chat-form) for field behavior, validation, and how answers are sent to the server. The form is configured with JavaScript; it has no `data-*` attributes.

Cloudflare Worker Full Example

A production-ready Cloudflare Worker with lead capture, a knowledge base, rate limits and budgets. Conversations live in D1 and the counters in a Durable Object, so every isolate and every region sees the same history and the same limits.

Installation > Widget (Client-Side) > Self-hosting

To serve the widget from your own site, copy `dist/chatcops.min.js`, `dist/chatcops.panel.js` and the `dist/chunks/` folder into the same folder. The loader finds the panel next to itself, and the panel finds its chunks. If you can only serve one file, use `dist/chatcops.full.min.js` instead: the whole chat in one script, loaded up front. A Content Security Policy needs the folder's origin in `script-src` either way.

Internationalization > Setting a Locale

The widget sends `locale` with every message, and the server asks the model to reply in that language.

Server Setup > Response format > The 0.5 format

Requests without `protocol` get plain chunks:

```
data: {"content":"Hello"}

data: {"content":" there"}

data: {"leadCaptured":true,"leadData":{"name":"Ada","email":"ada@example.com","projectDetails":"Support bot for an online store","source":"chatcops-widget"}}

data: {"done":true}

data: [DONE]
```

The stream can contain these chunks:

- `{"content":"..."}` for each text chunk.
- `{"leadCaptured":true,"leadData":{...}}` when the lead capture tool succeeds.
- `{"error":"rate_limit","retryAfter":12}` when the client is rate limited.
- `{"error":"provider_error"}` when the provider fails or can't be set up, when the model keeps calling tools past the limit, or when a reply is already being written for the same conversation.
- `{"error":"Invalid request","details":{...}}` when the request fails schema validation.
- `{"error":"internal_error"}` when the server hits an unexpected error.
- `{"done":true}` at the end of a successful reply.

Errors in this format are chunks in an HTTP 200 response, followed by `data: [DONE]`. A body that isn't JSON gets HTTP 400 `{"error":"Invalid JSON body"}`.

Storage > Retention > Cloudflare Workers

Add a `scheduled` export to your Worker. Cloudflare calls it on the cron triggers you define in `wrangler.toml`.

This example uses [`@chatcops/store-redis`](/server/storage/#redis) with Upstash's HTTP-based Redis client because it runs directly in Workers over HTTP without extra database-connection setup:

```bash
npm install @chatcops/store-redis @upstash/redis
```

Create a fresh handler inside `scheduled()` using the invocation's `env` so that no environment-specific secret is cached at global scope:

Internationalization > Available Locales

| Code | Language |
|------|----------|
| `ar` | Arabic |
| `en` | English (default, built in) |
| `de` | German |
| `es` | Spanish |
| `fr` | French |
| `he` | Hebrew |
| `hi` | Hindi |
| `it` | Italian |
| `ja` | Japanese |
| `ko` | Korean |
| `nl` | Dutch |
| `pt` | Portuguese (Brazil) |
| `ur` | Urdu |
| `zh` | Chinese (Simplified) |

Any other `locale` uses the English strings, with your `strings` on top. Hindi is loaded as a separate file only when requested. To add a language, see `packages/widget/src/locales/README.md` and [#55](https://github.com/codercops/chatcops/issues/55).

Protocol > Part Reference > WirePart Details and Examples

#### `start`
Always the first event in a successful stream:

```json
{
  "type": "start",
  "protocol": 1,
  "conversationId": "c_8f2",
  "messageId": "m_91a0c4",
  "capabilities": {
    "session": true
  }
}
```

- `capabilities.session`: When `true`, indicates that session tokens are enabled on the server. When `allowAnonymous: true` is also set, chat requests without a token can still proceed.

#### `text-start`, `text-delta`, `text-end`
Surrounds and streams chunks of assistant text:

```json
{ "type": "text-start", "id": "t1" }
```

```json
{ "type": "text-delta", "id": "t1", "delta": "Hello! How can I help you today?" }
```

```json
{ "type": "text-end", "id": "t1" }
```

#### `source`
Sent when a `knowledge` source has `retrieve()` and the reply cites a chunk from it, at most once per page. `sourceId` is the page's `source.id`, and `snippet` is the chunk's text with whitespace collapsed, cut to 200 characters. Citations the model provider returns natively come out as the same part:

```json
{
  "type": "source",
  "sourceId": "src_faq_1",
  "url": "https://example.com/docs/pricing",
  "title": "Pricing Documentation",
  "snippet": "Our Starter plan begins at $19/mo."
}
```

#### `tool-call`
Emitted when the assistant calls a tool:

```json
{
  "type": "tool-call",
  "toolCallId": "call_123",
  "toolName": "lookup_order",
  "input": { "orderId": "ORD-456" },
  "executor": "server"
}
```

- `executor`: Can be `'server'` (executed on the backend), `'client'` (dispatched to the client app), or `'mcp'` (executed via an MCP server).

#### `tool-result`
Emitted after tool execution completes:

```json
{
  "type": "tool-result",
  "toolCallId": "call_123",
  "output": { "status": "shipped", "tracking": "TRK987654" }
}
```

#### `lead-captured`
Emitted when visitor contact details are captured:

```json
{
  "type": "lead-captured",
  "lead": {
    "name": "Jane Doe",
    "email": "jane@example.com",
    "projectDetails": "Need custom chatbot integration"
  }
}
```

Quick Start

Get ChatCops running in three steps: add the widget, set up a server, and start chatting.

Theming > Position

The widget supports two positions:

- `bottom-right` (default) — FAB and panel anchored to bottom-right
- `bottom-left` — FAB and panel anchored to bottom-left

On mobile screens, the chat panel always goes full-screen regardless of position.

Server Setup > Budgets

Tokens count input and output at face value, and every request sends the conversation so far, so a long conversation uses up a token budget faster than its length suggests. Budgets are checked before each model request and charged after it, so a reply can go over by one request, and each request asks for no more output than is left. A used-up budget ends the reply with an error instead of calling the model, and the server logs which one.

The per-IP budget needs the visitor's IP, so it's skipped for requests where the adapter can't tell.

For persistent conversations, custom stores, Postgres, Redis, and the storage capabilities available to the server, see [the storage page](/server/storage/).

Cloudflare Worker Full Example > Widget HTML

```html
<script
  src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@chatcops/widget/dist/chatcops.min.js"
  data-api-url="https://chatcops-worker.your-subdomain.workers.dev"
  data-accent="#6366f1"
  data-brand-name="AI Support"
  data-welcome-message="Hi! How can I help?"
></script>
```

Upgrading from 0.5

This release changes a lot inside the server: how replies are run and stored, how limits are counted, and what goes over the wire. Most apps upgrade without code changes, because old widgets keep working against the new server and the new widget keeps working against an old server. This page lists what can need your attention, then the new options worth turning on.

The versions are `@chatcops/server` 0.6, `@chatcops/widget` 0.6 and `@chatcops/core` 0.5. They need Node.js 22 or later.

Storage > Retention > Vercel Cron Jobs

:::note
Vercel Cron Jobs are available on all plans. On the Hobby plan, each cron job is limited to running at most once per day, which is sufficient for daily retention cleanup.
:::

Next.js, Hono, Bun and Deno > Checking your setup

With the server running (a placeholder key such as `test` is enough for the first two):

```bash
# CORS preflight: expect 204 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin
curl -i -X OPTIONS http://localhost:3000/api/chat

# Broken JSON: expect 400 {"error":"Invalid JSON body"}
curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/chat -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{broken'

# A real reply (needs a real key): expect data: lines, ending with data: [DONE]
curl -N -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/chat -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"conversationId":"test","message":"Hello"}'
```

API Reference > Methods > `ChatCops.destroy()`

Completely remove the widget from the DOM and clean up all event listeners.

- **Popup mode:** Removes FAB, panel, and welcome bubble from the page.
- **Inline mode:** Removes the widget from the container element.

```typescript
ChatCops.destroy();
```

Testing your bot

A change to the system prompt, the model or the knowledge base can quietly break an answer that used to be right. `chatcops test` catches that. You write the conversations your bot has to get right in YAML, say what each reply should contain, and the command runs them against your bot and tells you which ones broke.

```bash
npx chatcops test
```

It exits 0 when every test passed, 1 when some failed, and 2 when it couldn't run (a bad eval file, a missing config), so it works as a CI step.

Server Setup > Request Schema

The server validates incoming requests with Zod:

```typescript
interface ChatRequest {
  conversationId: string,  // 1-128 chars
  message: string,         // 1-10000 chars
  messageId?: string,      // Optional, 1-128 chars
  protocol?: 1,            // Optional, asks for protocol v1 (see Response format)
  regenerate?: boolean | { assistantMessageId: string },  // Optional
  pageContext?: {           // Optional page context
    url: string,           // Valid URL (the prompt gets the first 2000 chars)
    title: string,         // Max 500 chars
    description?: string,  // Max 1000 chars
    contentSnippet?: string, // Max 2000 chars
    data?: { [key: string]: string },  // From the widget's setContext(): max 20 fields, keys 40 chars, values 500
  },
  locale?: string,         // Max 10 chars
  userData?: {              // Optional pre-chat data, max 50 fields
    [key: string]: string,  // Key max 100 chars, value max 500 chars
  },
}
```

The widget sends pre-chat answers in `userData`. See the [pre-chat form guide](/widget/pre-chat-form) for how the widget collects and submits these answers. Use the `preChatFields` option in [`ChatCopsServerConfig`](#chatcopsserverconfig) to limit which fields the server keeps.

Vercel Adapter > Widget Configuration

Point the widget to your Vercel deployment:

```html
<script
  src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@chatcops/widget/dist/chatcops.min.js"
  data-api-url="https://your-app.vercel.app/api/chat"
></script>
```

Testing your bot > Unit tests with a scripted model

Each model step takes the next entry of the script:

- `textStep(text, { chunkSize, usage })` streams `text` in pieces of `chunkSize` characters (8 by default).
- `toolStep(calls, { text })` calls tools, optionally after some text.
- A list of provider events, or a function that builds them from the step's params, for anything else.
- An `Error` makes that step fail, and `'hang'` waits until the request is aborted, for testing disconnects.

`scriptedProvider(script, { delayMs })` waits `delayMs` before each event, to test timeouts and streaming. `citations: 'native'` makes it act like Claude, getting `sources` on each step. `provider.calls` keeps the params of every step, with the messages as they were then.

Protocol > Errors During Streaming > `error` WirePart Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | `WireErrorCode` | The error identifier (e.g. `'provider_error'`, `'budget_exceeded'`, `'timeout'`, `'tool_error'`, `'content_filtered'`, `'internal_error'`). |
| `retryable` | `boolean` | **Required.** Indicates whether the client should attempt to retry the request. |
| `message` | `string` | Optional human-readable description of the error. |
| `retryAfterMs` | `number` | Optional delay in milliseconds before retrying. |
| `scope` | `'conversation' \| 'session' \| 'ip' \| 'global'` | Optional scope of the limit. Used when `code` is `'budget_exceeded'` to identify which limit was reached. |

#### Budget Exceeded In-Stream Error

When a server budget (token, message, or USD cost limit) is exceeded:

```json
{
  "type": "error",
  "code": "budget_exceeded",
  "retryable": false,
  "scope": "conversation"
}
```

---

Upgrading to 1.0 > `@chatcops/server` > The `RateLimiter` export is gone

The server stopped using it in 0.6: limits are counted in `storage`, set with the `rateLimit` option, so they hold across instances. If your own code used `new RateLimiter({ maxRequests, windowMs })` directly, the replacement is `createRateLimiter(counters, { limit, windowMs })` from `@chatcops/core`. It works on any `CounterStore`, such as `memoryStorage().counters`, and its `check(key)` returns a promise.

Widget Configuration > Script Tag Attribute Reference

| Attribute | Config Key | Description |
|-----------|-----------|-------------|
| `data-api-url` | `apiUrl` | API endpoint URL (required) |
| `data-mode` | `mode` | `'popup'` or `'inline'` |
| `data-container` | `container` | CSS selector for inline container |
| `data-theme-mode` | `theme.mode` | `'light'`, `'dark'` or `'auto'` |
| `data-accent` | `theme.accent` | Primary accent color |
| `data-accent-dark` | `theme.accentDark` | Accent color in dark mode |
| `data-text-color` | `theme.textColor` | Primary text color |
| `data-bg-color` | `theme.bgColor` | Background color |
| `data-font-family` | `theme.fontFamily` | Font family |
| `data-border-radius` | `theme.borderRadius` | Border radius. A bare number is px (`12`), or use any CSS length (`1rem`) |
| `data-position` | `theme.position` | `'bottom-right'` or `'bottom-left'` |
| `data-brand-name` | `branding.name` | Header title |
| `data-brand-avatar` | `branding.avatar` | Avatar image URL |
| `data-brand-subtitle` | `branding.subtitle` | Subtitle text |
| `data-welcome-message` | `welcomeMessage` | First assistant message |
| `data-disclosure` | `disclosure` | `"false"` turns the AI disclosure off |
| `data-disclosure-text` | `disclosure.text` | Wording of the AI disclosure |
| `data-disclosure-url` | `disclosure.learnMoreUrl` | "Learn more" link in the AI disclosure |
| `data-welcome-bubble` | `welcomeBubble.text` | Welcome bubble text |
| `data-welcome-bubble-delay` | `welcomeBubble.delay` | Bubble delay in ms |
| `data-placeholder` | `placeholder` | Input placeholder |
| `data-auto-open` | `autoOpen` | Auto-open delay in ms or `true` |
| `data-locale` | `locale` | Language code |
| `data-dir` | `dir` | Text direction: `'ltr'`, `'rtl'` or `'auto'` |
| `data-persistence` | `persistence` | `'local'`, `'session'` or `'none'` |
| `data-history-ttl-days` | `historyTtlDays` | Days a saved conversation is kept |
| `data-turnstile-site-key` | `turnstileSiteKey` | Cloudflare Turnstile site key, when the server checks Turnstile |
| `data-user-token` | `userToken` | Signed token for a signed-in visitor, when the server has `identity` set |

Theming > ThemeConfig Interface

```typescript
interface ThemeConfig {
  mode?: 'light' | 'dark' | 'auto';  // Default 'auto': follows the system setting
  accent?: string;          // Hex color
  accentDark?: string;      // Hex color, the accent in dark mode. Defaults to accent
  textColor?: string;       // Hex color
  bgColor?: string;         // Hex color
  fontFamily?: string;      // CSS font-family string
  borderRadius?: string | number;  // px if a number or numeric string (12, '12'), or any CSS length ('1rem')
  position?: 'bottom-right' | 'bottom-left';
}
```

AI Providers > Options

The server config's `maxTokens` (default 4096) and `temperature` are passed to the provider on every request.

Express Adapter > Express Compatibility

The adapter works with both Express 4.x and 5.x. Express is listed as an optional peer dependency — install it separately:

```bash
npm install express @chatcops/server
```

Widget Configuration > Inline Mode Behavior

When using `mode: 'inline'`:

- The chat panel renders inside the specified container element
- No floating action button (FAB) is created
- No welcome bubble is shown
- The panel is visible immediately (no toggle needed)
- `autoOpen` is ignored (always open)
- The panel fills 100% width and height of the container
- Mobile responsive overrides do not apply — the container controls sizing
- `open()` and `close()` still work programmatically

Pre-chat Form > What happens to answers

The widget includes the answers as `userData` on the next chat request. If that request fails, it sends the answers again with the retry. The server accepts at most 50 fields, with field names up to 100 characters and values up to 500 characters.

The server saves the answers with the conversation's first message and uses those saved answers for the rest of the conversation; later requests cannot replace them. Configure the server's [`preChatFields` allowlist](/server/setup#chatcopsserverconfig) to keep only the fields your server needs.

Pre-chat Form > Form options > Field options

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | Required key for the answer. Use `name` to personalize the welcome message or `message` to start the chat with the visitor's answer. |
| `type` | `'text' \| 'email' \| 'select' \| 'textarea'` | Required input type. Email fields are checked for a valid email format. |
| `label` | `string` | Required text label displayed above the field. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | Optional placeholder. For a select, this replaces the default prompt. If omitted, the select prompt comes from `strings.selectPlaceholder` (English default: `Select {label}...`). |
| `required` | `boolean` | Optional. When `true`, the visitor must enter or select a non-empty value before submitting. Defaults to `false`. |
| `options` | `string[]` | Optional choices for a `select` field. |

Required fields are checked for non-empty values, and non-empty `email` fields are checked for email format. Invalid fields show an error and the form stays open until corrected. Values are trimmed before they are submitted.

ChatCops Documentation > Get Started

chunks.text:
Analytics

ChatCops includes a lightweight analytics collector that tracks conversation metrics server-side.

Protocol > Errors During Streaming

If a failure occurs **after** the SSE stream has already opened and sent a `start` part, the server cannot change the HTTP status code (since headers have already been sent).

Instead, the server emits an `error` part followed by a `finish` part with reason `'error'`, and then closes with `data: [DONE]`:

```text
data: {"type":"error","code":"provider_error","retryable":true}

data: {"type":"finish","reason":"error"}

data: [DONE]

```

AI SDK (useChat) > How it differs from an AI SDK route

The server keeps the history. A typical AI SDK route takes the whole `messages` array from the client and sends it to the model. ChatCops reads only the last user message and answers from the conversation it has stored, so a visitor can't edit the history or add assistant turns the model never wrote. Changing an earlier message in the client changes what's on screen, not what the model sees.

The rest maps over directly:

- `regenerate()` replaces the answer on the server too. The old answer stays until the new one has finished.
- A retry of a message that already has an answer gets that answer again, without calling the model.
- Tools run on the server. They show up as `tool-<name>` parts with `providerExecuted: true`, so `useChat` doesn't try to run them or wait for their output.
- A lead from the lead capture tool arrives as a `data-lead-captured` part.
- Each assistant message has `metadata.conversationId`. With `exposeUsage: true` the metadata also has the reply's token `usage`.
- A request the server won't answer (rate limited, invalid, a reply already streaming) gets an HTTP status with a JSON body. An error after the reply has started, such as `provider_error` or `budget_exceeded`, is an `error` chunk with the code as its text. Both set `useChat`'s `error` and call its `onError`.

To send ChatCops' visitor context, put it in the request body. `pageContext`, `locale` and `userData` pass through:

```tsx
sendMessage({ text: input }, { body: { locale: navigator.language } });
```

chunks.text:
Protocol > Stream Format and Framing

Protocol v1 uses HTTP Server-Sent Events (SSE). Successful streaming replies return with HTTP `200 OK` and headers:

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform
X-Accel-Buffering: no
x-chatcops-protocol: 1
Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Retry-After, X-ChatCops-Protocol
```

Protocol > Stream Format and Framing > Event Framing Rules

1. **SSE Data Lines**: Every protocol event is serialized as JSON on a line starting with `data: `, terminated by a double newline (`\n\n`):

   ```text
   data: {"type":"text-delta","id":"t1","delta":"Hello"}

   ```

2. **Terminal Stream Marker**: The server terminates every cleanly completed stream with the literal SSE frame:

   ```text
   data: [DONE]

   ```

3. **Heartbeat / Ping Comments**: After 10 seconds of silence (e.g. while awaiting a slow tool or backend operation), the server sends an SSE comment line:

   ```text
   : ping

   ```

   Comments begin with a colon `:` and do not contain JSON data. Custom clients should ignore them; they serve to prevent timeouts in intermediary proxies and firewalls.
4. **Distinction Between `finish` and `[DONE]`**:
   - `finish` is a **protocol part** that carries turn termination details (`reason`, token `usage`, pending calls).
   - `[DONE]` is the **SSE transport framing marker** indicating that the HTTP stream has ended.
   - If a stream closes or reaches EOF without emitting a `finish` event part, the stream was abruptly **interrupted or cut off** (e.g., server process crash, proxy timeout, network drop).
5. **Forward Compatibility**: Clients must ignore unknown or unrecognized `type` values in `WirePart` objects. The protocol design allows introducing new part types without breaking compliant clients.

---

Upgrading from 0.5 > Things to check > Smaller changes

- Each reply is saved as one assistant message with its parts (text, then each tool call and result), its status and token usage. A store written for 0.4 that only has `get`, `save` and `delete` keeps working; the server logs one warning that two instances writing the same conversation can lose a message, which stores with `append` avoid.
- A reply the visitor walked away from is saved and marked `aborted`, and the model doesn't see it next time.
- Retrying a message that already has a saved reply sends that reply again instead of asking the model for a second one.
- Knowledge base excerpts, the visitor's page and pre-chat details, and the locale line go after the system prompt instead of into it. That lets Claude's prompt cache hold your system prompt, and keeps visitor text out of the instructions.
- Pre-chat form answers are stored with the conversation from its first message and can't change after that. `preChatFields` lists the fields to keep.
- A provider that fails to set up (a missing API key, say) no longer stops the process at startup. It's logged once, and chat requests get `provider_error`.
- `require('@chatcops/widget')` now fails with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`. It never worked (it returned an empty object). Use `import`.
- Tool `execute(input, context)` gets a second argument with the conversation id and an abort signal. Tools that ignore it keep working.

Cloudflare Workers Adapter

The Cloudflare adapter creates a handler compatible with the Workers runtime.

Protocol > Try It with curl

You can test a running ChatCops server using `curl`.

Next.js, Hono, Bun and Deno > The visitor's IP

Rate limits and the per-IP budget key on the visitor's IP. The handler only reads it from a header that the platform sets itself, because a visitor can send any `X-Forwarded-For` they like and get a fresh limit with every request.

| Where it runs | Where the IP comes from |
|---|---|
| Vercel | Vercel's own headers (`x-vercel-forwarded-for`, `x-real-ip`, `x-forwarded-for`), which Vercel overwrites. Nothing to set. |
| Cloudflare Workers (`chatcopsCloudflareHandler`) | `CF-Connecting-IP`. Nothing to set. |
| Express | `req.ip`, which follows Express's `trust proxy` setting. Behind one proxy, call `app.set('trust proxy', 1)`. |
| Anywhere else | Your `clientIp` function. |

Anywhere else, set `clientIp` to read the header your host or proxy sets:

```typescript
import { chatcopsVercelHandler } from '@chatcops/server';

const handler = chatcopsVercelHandler({
  provider: { type: 'claude', apiKey: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY! },
  systemPrompt: 'Be helpful.',
  clientIp: (req) => req.headers.get('x-nf-client-connection-ip'), // Netlify
  // clientIp: (req) => req.headers.get('x-real-ip'),            // your nginx, with proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr
});
```

Bun and Deno have no proxy in front, so the examples above copy the socket address into a header and read that. With Hono, do the same in the route with Hono's `getConnInfo`, or read your proxy's header.

Without a way to tell the IP, per-IP limits are skipped and the server logs one warning saying so. Visitors never share one limit: that used to happen with an `"unknown"` key, where one busy visitor could use up the limit for everyone.

Protocol > Errors Before Streaming > Pre-Stream Error Statuses

| HTTP Status | Error Code (`WireErrorCode` or string) | Trigger Condition | Message / Response Body |
|---|---|---|---|
| `400` | `invalid_request` | The request body failed Zod schema validation or JSON parsing. | Lists invalid field paths (e.g. `"Invalid request: message"`), never input values. |
| `401` | `session_required` | Session tokens are required and the request had no token, an invalid signature, or a token issued for another origin. | `{"error":{"code":"session_required","message":"..."}}`. Obtain a token for this conversation from `<chat url>/session`. |
| `401` | `token_expired` | The provided session token has expired. | Request a new token from `<chat url>/session`. |
| `401` | `conversation_mismatch` | The session token is valid but was issued for a different conversation. | Obtain a token for the current conversation from `<chat url>/session`. |
| `401` | `turnstile_failed` | `/session` endpoint only: Cloudflare Turnstile verification failed or was missing. | Returned when bot protection challenge fails. |
| `403` | `origin_not_allowed` | The `Origin` header is not permitted by `allowedOrigins`. | Answered before the request body is parsed. Returns legacy format `{"error":"origin_not_allowed"}`. |
| `405` | `Method not allowed` | An HTTP method other than `POST` or `OPTIONS` was used on the chat endpoint. | Answered before the request body is parsed, with `Allow: POST, OPTIONS`. Returns legacy format `{"error":"Method not allowed"}`. |
| `409` | `conversation_busy` | Another reply is currently being generated for this `conversationId`. | The server locks conversation turns to prevent state races. |
| `413` | `payload_too_large` | The request body exceeds the maximum permitted size (default 256 KB). | Prevents excessive memory allocation. |
| `429` | `rate_limited` | The client IP has exceeded the configured request rate limit. | Includes `retryAfterMs` in body and `Retry-After` in HTTP headers. |
| `500` | `internal_error` | An unexpected server error occurred prior to stream initialization. | Generic catch-all failure. |
| `503` | `provider_unavailable` | The AI provider failed setup or is not reachable (e.g. missing API key). | Server logs the underlying reason at startup. |

Testing your bot > Recorded replays > GitHub Actions

```yaml
name: Evals
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  evals:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: 22 }
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npx chatcops test
```

Installation > Widget (Client-Side) > CDN (Recommended)

The simplest way — no build step required:

```html
<script
  src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@chatcops/widget/dist/chatcops.min.js"
  data-api-url="https://your-api.com/chat"
></script>
```

`chatcops.min.js` is a small loader (about 3 kB) that draws the chat button. The rest of the chat (`chatcops.panel.js`, next to it) downloads when the visitor hovers or clicks the button, or when the chat has to open on its own. So pages where nobody opens the chat only pay for the button. Parts that only some sites use, the pre-chat form and Turnstile, are separate files in `dist/chunks/` and download only on sites that turn them on.

Server Setup > Response format > Protocol v1

Protocol v1 is the default stream format for modern ChatCops clients. Replies stream as typed Server-Sent Events (SSE) carrying granular event parts, with pre-stream refusals returned as JSON with standard HTTP error statuses.

For the full specification covering format negotiation, request fields, SSE framing, all 13 wire part variants, and HTTP error mappings, see the [Protocol Reference](/server/protocol/).

Knowledge Base > FAQ Knowledge Source

Best for structured question-answer pairs:

```typescript
import { FAQKnowledgeSource } from '@chatcops/core';

const faq = new FAQKnowledgeSource([
  { question: 'What are your business hours?', answer: '9am-5pm EST, Monday to Friday.' },
  { question: 'Do you offer refunds?', answer: 'Yes, full refunds within 30 days.' },
  { question: 'How do I contact support?', answer: 'Email support@example.com or use this chat!' },
  { question: 'What payment methods do you accept?', answer: 'Visa, Mastercard, PayPal, and wire transfer.' },
]);
```

API Reference

The `ChatCops` singleton is exposed on `window.ChatCops` by the script tag build (`chatcops.min.js` or `chatcops.full.min.js`), or importable from the ESM bundle.

AI Providers > Options

| Option | Providers | Default | What it does |
|--------|-----------|---------|--------------|
| `type` | all | none | `'claude'`, `'openai'`, `'gemini'`, `'openai-compatible'`, or the name of a [custom provider](#custom-providers). |
| `apiKey` | all | none | Required for Claude, OpenAI and Gemini. Optional for `openai-compatible`. |
| `model` | all | see above | The model id. Required for `openai-compatible`. |
| `effort` | all | `'low'` | How much effort the model spends per reply: `'low'`, `'medium'`, `'high'`, `'xhigh'` or `'max'`. Lower is faster and cheaper, which suits chat. Sent as `output_config.effort` to Claude 4.6 and later, `reasoning_effort` to OpenAI reasoning models, and `thinkingLevel` to Gemini 3 models. Models without an effort setting ignore it. |
| `baseURL` | all | provider default | A custom API endpoint: a proxy, a gateway, or an OpenAI-compatible server. Required for `openai-compatible`. |
| `headers` | OpenAI, openai-compatible | none | Extra headers sent on every request. |
| `supportsTools` | OpenAI, openai-compatible | `true` | Set to `false` for a model that can't call tools. Tools aren't sent, and one warning is logged. |
| `fetch` | all | the global `fetch` | The `fetch` the provider SDK sends requests with. Use it to route requests through a proxy, or to replay recorded responses in tests. |
| `promptCaching` | Claude | `true` | Marks the system prompt and tools as a cached prefix, so later requests read them from Claude's prompt cache at about a tenth of the input price. Prompts shorter than the model's cache minimum aren't cached either way. OpenAI and Gemini cache long prompts on their own. |
| `organization` | OpenAI | none | Your OpenAI organization id. |
| `maxTokensParam` | OpenAI, openai-compatible | `'max_completion_tokens'` for `openai`, `'max_tokens'` for `openai-compatible` | The name of the output token limit sent to the API. |

Testing your bot > Recorded replays

A few things to know about recordings:

- Headers aren't saved, and neither are query parameters like `key` or `api_key`. API keys usually travel in one of those, so they stay out of the files. The request and response bodies are saved, which means your system prompt and the replies are in the files, so treat them like the rest of your code. Request bodies stay readable JSON, so a re-recording's diff shows what you changed. Responses over 4 kB, such as a streamed reply with one event per token, are saved gzipped in base64, which keeps the files about a tenth of the size.
- `repeat` records every run, and replay plays them back in the same order.
- Replays answer at once, so `latency` in a replayed run is not the real latency.

Knowledge Base > Citations

When knowledge sources return chunks (through `retrieve`), answers say which pages they came from. Each page the reply cites becomes a `source` part in the stream, once per page, after the text that cites it, and is saved with the reply:

```json
{ "type": "source", "sourceId": "https://example.com/pricing", "url": "https://example.com/pricing", "title": "Pricing", "snippet": "The Team plan costs $20 per user per month…" }
```

How the model cites depends on the provider:

| Provider | Sources go to the model as | Citations come back as |
|---|---|---|
| Claude | `search_result` blocks before the visitor's message | Claude's own citations, mapped to `source` parts |
| OpenAI, Gemini, others | A numbered `<sources>` block in the system context | `[1]`, `[2]` in the text; numbers that match no source are removed |

Either way, retrieved text is framed as reference material that never contains instructions, and it can't add or unlock tools. Sources with only `getContext` work as before: their text goes in the context, without citations.

Theming > Light, dark and auto

The widget has a light and a dark look. By default (`mode: 'auto'`) it follows the visitor's system setting, and switches while the page is open when that setting changes. Pin one with `mode`:

```typescript
ChatCops.init({
  apiUrl: '/api/chat',
  theme: {
    mode: 'light',               // 'light', 'dark' or 'auto' (the default)
    accent: '#4f46e5',           // buttons, the launcher, visitor messages
    accentDark: '#a5b4fc',       // the accent in dark mode; defaults to accent
    fontFamily: 'Inter, sans-serif',
    borderRadius: 12,            // px if a number, or any CSS length like '1rem'
    position: 'bottom-right',    // or 'bottom-left'
  },
});
```

On the script tag, these are `data-theme-mode`, `data-accent` and `data-accent-dark`.

| Element | Light | Dark |
|---------|-------|------|
| Background | `#ffffff` | `#0a0a0a` |
| Surface (bot messages, header) | `#f4f5f7` | `#1a1a1a` |
| Input area | `#ffffff` | `#2a2a2a` |
| Border | `#d9dce1` | `#333333` |
| Text | `#1a1d23` | `#ffffff` |
| Secondary text | `#5b616e` | `#a0a0a0` |
| Accent | `#4f46e5` | `#6366f1` |
| Errors | `#c62828` | `#ef4444` |

The dark look is the one the widget had before light mode existed. Text on the accent is picked for contrast (white or near-black, with the accent darkened a little when neither reaches 4.5:1), in each mode for its own accent.

Security > Before you go live

The server logs one line about these settings when it starts, and an error or warning for the mistakes it can spot: an origin without `https://` or with a path, an `http://` origin that isn't local, a session secret that's also in a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` (or `VITE_`, `PUBLIC_` and so on) variable. For example:

```
[chatcops] ERROR: Allowed origin "acme.com" must start with http:// or https://.
[chatcops] Security: chat allowed from acme.com; session tokens on (900s); Turnstile off.
```

Then go through the list:

- `allowedOrigins` lists your sites, and nothing else. `['*']` is the default.
- `storage` is a store package, so limits and budgets hold across instances.
- `budgets.globalPerDay` is set to a number you're fine paying on a bad day.
- `sessionSecrets` is set, from a secret store, never a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` or `VITE_` variable. Set `allowAnonymous: true` with it if widgets before 0.6 are still cached on your pages, and drop it after a few days.
- On a host other than Vercel, Cloudflare or Express, `clientIp` reads your platform's header. Otherwise per-IP limits are skipped.
- If you use the analytics endpoint, `analyticsToken` is set. Without it the endpoint is public.
- Each tool checks its own input. The model writes it, and a visitor can steer the model, so treat a tool's input like a form submission: check ids belong to the visitor, and keep write actions behind your own auth.
- Your system prompt says what the bot should refuse. None of these layers stop a visitor talking the model into off-topic work within your budget.

The details of each option are on the [server setup page](/server/setup/): [allowed origins](/server/setup/#allowed-origins), [session tokens](/server/setup/#session-tokens), [Turnstile](/server/setup/#turnstile) and [budgets](/server/setup/#budgets).

Protocol > Errors Before Streaming > Retry-After Header Behavior

When `retryAfterMs` is provided on rate-limited responses:
- The JSON response body includes `retryAfterMs` (in milliseconds).
- The HTTP response includes a `Retry-After` header expressing the waiting period in **seconds**, rounded up using `Math.ceil(retryAfterMs / 1000)`:

  ```http
  Retry-After: 42
  ```

Testing your bot > Eval files

Two assertions check what ChatCops adds to a reply:

- `cites` takes a URL glob, or a list of them, and each has to match a page the reply cites (`cites: "https://acme.test/pricing*"`). Globs work the same as in `ingest.include`. `cites: true` means it cites at least one page.
- `lead-captured: true` means the turn captured a lead. An object, such as `lead-captured: { email: jane@acme.test }`, also has to match those fields of the lead.

Two assertions check tool calls made during a turn:

- `calls-tool` asserts that the bot called a tool. It takes either a tool name (`calls-tool: lookup_order`) or `{ name, args }` to also check inputs (`calls-tool: { name: lookup_order, args: { id: "A-1001" } }`). Arguments match partially: every specified key must match, nested objects follow the same rule, extra input keys are allowed, and arrays must match exactly.
- `no-tool-call: true` asserts that no tool was called during the turn. It also takes a tool name (`no-tool-call: cancel_order`) to assert that the specific tool was not called, even if other tools were called.

A test can also set:

- `pageContext`: the page the visitor is on (`url`, `title`, and optionally `description` and `contentSnippet`)
- `locale` and `userData`, as the widget would send them
- `mocks.tools`: a fixed result for a server tool, so the test doesn't place a real order or send a real email
- `repeat` and `passRate`: run the test several times and pass when that share of runs passed (models aren't deterministic)

`defaults` at the top of the file applies to every test in it. A test's own values win, and tool mocks are merged:

Express Full Example > Environment Variables

```bash
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
CHATCOPS_SESSION_SECRET=...   # openssl rand -base64 32
WEBHOOK_URL=https://hooks.example.com/chatcops
WEBHOOK_SECRET=your-webhook-secret
ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://your-website.com
PORT=3001
```

Knowledge Base > Text Knowledge Source

Best for unstructured content (documentation, product descriptions, policies):

```typescript
import { TextKnowledgeSource } from '@chatcops/core';

const docs = new TextKnowledgeSource([
  `Our company was founded in 2020 by Jane Doe.
  We specialize in AI-powered customer support solutions.
  Our flagship product is ChatCops, an embeddable chatbot widget.
  We serve over 500 businesses worldwide.
  Our headquarters is in San Francisco, CA.`,
]);
```

Internationalization > Setting a Locale > With a bundler

The ESM build doesn't fetch translations itself. Import the one you need from `@chatcops/widget/locales/<code>` and pass it as `strings`, for example `import de from '@chatcops/widget/locales/de'` and then `ChatCops.init({ apiUrl: '/api/chat', locale: 'de', strings: de })`.

The single-file build (`chatcops.full.min.js`) loads nothing else, so pass `strings` there too.

Drop a single `<script>` tag into your HTML. The widget auto-initializes and appears as a floating button in the bottom-right corner.

The widget accepts configuration via `data-*` attributes:

| Attribute | Description | Default |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| `data-api-url` | Your server endpoint (required) | — |
| `data-accent` | Primary accent color | `#6366f1` |
| `data-brand-name` | Name shown in chat header | `"AI Assistant"` |

| `data-position` | `bottom-right` or `bottom-left` | `bottom-right` |

Protocol > Request Body > Nested Request Structures

#### `pageContext`
Provides current webpage context to the assistant. The server validates:
- `url`: Valid URL string (`z.string().url()`). Only up to 2,000 characters reach the prompt.
- `title`: String, maximum 500 characters.
- `description` *(optional)*: String, maximum 1,000 characters.
- `contentSnippet` *(optional)*: String, maximum 2,000 characters.
- `data` *(optional)*: Details the site added with the widget's `setContext()`, at most 20 string fields, keys up to 40 characters and values up to 500. They reach the model as page details that aren't verified.

```json
{
  "url": "https://example.com/pricing",
  "title": "Pricing & Plans - Acme Inc",
  "description": "Flexible plans starting at $19/mo.",
  "contentSnippet": "Starter: $19/mo. Pro: $49/mo. Enterprise: Custom."
}
```

AI Providers

ChatCops puts every provider behind the same `AIProvider` interface. Switch between Claude, OpenAI, and Gemini by changing one config value.

API Reference > Methods > `ChatCops.version`

The widget's version, such as `"0.7.0"`.

Upgrading from 0.5 > Things to check > Budgets are on by default

The server now caps what replies can cost: 200 replies per conversation and 2 million tokens per IP per UTC day. A visitor who hits a cap gets an error instead of a reply. The server logs the budgets in force when it starts. To change one, set it in `budgets`. To turn one off, set it to `false`. `budgets: false` turns them all off. See [Budgets](/server/setup/#budgets).

Protocol > Protocol Negotiation > Detecting the Protocol v1 Response

When protocol v1 is active:
- **Successful streaming responses** include the response header:

  ```http
  x-chatcops-protocol: 1
  ```

  and the stream begins with a `start` event part: `data: {"type":"start",...}`.
- **Cross-origin requests** allow clients to inspect this header because the server exposes `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Retry-After, X-ChatCops-Protocol`.
- **Pre-stream refusals** are returned immediately as non-200 JSON responses (for example, `400 Bad Request` or `429 Too Many Requests`).

If neither `"protocol": 1` in the body nor `x-chatcops-protocol: 1` in the request header is supplied, the server falls back to the legacy 0.5 response format (where all refusals and text chunks are framed in a 200 SSE stream).

chunks.text:
Protocol

ChatCops protocol v1 is the client-server protocol used by the `@chatcops/widget` (version 0.6 and newer) and custom clients, including mobile apps, command-line tools, backend services, and alternative frontends.

This reference specifies how clients negotiate protocol v1, the JSON request body schema and limits, Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming framing, every wire part event, and HTTP error handling.

---

Internationalization > Server-Side i18n

The server doesn't translate anything itself. When a request has a `locale`, it adds this line to the system prompt:

```text
Reply in the visitor's language. Their browser locale is es.
```

Error messages the visitor sees come from the widget's `strings`:

| Key | Shown when | English |
|---|---|---|
| `errorRateLimit` | Too many messages, and the server didn't say for how long | Too many messages. Please wait a moment. |
| `errorRateLimitWait` | Too many messages, with the server's wait (`{seconds}`) | Too many messages. Please try again in \{seconds\} seconds. |
| `errorBudget` | The conversation used up its budget | This chat has reached its limit. |
| `errorBudgetDaily` | The visitor's or the site's daily budget is used up | The assistant has reached its limit for today. Please try again later. |
| `errorUnavailable` | The server couldn't set up the AI provider (a missing key, say) | The assistant is unavailable right now. Please try again later. |
| `errorCutOff` | The reply stopped before the server said it was done | The reply was cut off. |
| `errorNetwork` | The request failed or timed out | Connection error. Please check your network. |
| `errorGeneric` | Anything else | Something went wrong. Please try again. |

The limit and cut-off messages need a 0.6 server, which sends the reason. With an older server, the widget falls back to `errorRateLimit`, `errorNetwork` and `errorGeneric`. The server config's `i18n` option is deprecated: the server ignores it and logs a warning when it's set, and it will be removed in a later release.

API Reference > Methods > `ChatCops.newConversation()`

Start a fresh conversation: a new conversation id, and the chat back to the welcome message. A reply that's still coming is stopped. Pre-chat answers are kept, so the visitor isn't asked again.

```typescript
ChatCops.newConversation();
```

Protocol > Protocol Negotiation > Requesting Protocol v1

A client requests protocol v1 using either of two supported mechanisms:

1. **Request Body Field (Recommended)**:
   Include `"protocol": 1` in the JSON request body:

   ```json
   {
     "protocol": 1,
     "conversationId": "test-1",
     "message": "Hi"
   }
   ```

   A request body field is preferred over a custom header because custom headers trigger a CORS preflight request, whereas older servers before v0.6 only allowed `Content-Type` in their preflights.

2. **Request Header**:
   Send the `x-chatcops-protocol` header with value `1` (or any integer 1 or higher):

   ```http
   x-chatcops-protocol: 1
   ```

Knowledge Base > Text Knowledge Source > How Text Matching Works

1. Each string in the array is one chunk
2. User's query words are matched against each chunk
3. Top 3 relevant chunks are returned
4. Context is prefixed with `"Relevant context:\n"`
