chunks.text:
Security > Always on

These need no config:

- Visitor-supplied text (the page URL and title, pre-chat answers) goes into a separate block marked as untrusted data, never into your system prompt. It's capped at 4,000 characters.
- Pre-chat answers are stored with the first message and can't be changed later in the conversation. `preChatFields` drops any field you didn't ask for.
- Request bodies over 256 KB get `413`, and every field has a length cap.
- Tool definitions are checked when the server starts, and a tool call whose arguments aren't valid JSON gets an error result instead of running.
- Webhook URLs that point at private or link-local addresses (including cloud metadata endpoints like `169.254.169.254`) are refused unless the webhook sets `allowPrivateNetwork: true`. Only literal addresses are checked, so also block private ranges at the network level if you can.
- The visitor's IP is read only from headers your platform sets, never from an `X-Forwarded-For` a visitor can send. See [the visitor's IP](/server/fetch-runtimes/#the-visitors-ip).

Security > A production config > The widget

With `turnstile` on the server, give the widget the site key. Nothing else changes, since the widget handles sessions on its own:

```html
<script
  src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@chatcops/widget/dist/chatcops.min.js"
  data-api-url="https://acme.com/api/chat"
  data-turnstile-site-key="0x4AAAAAAA..."
></script>
```

Upgrading to 1.0

1.0 removes the options and methods that 0.6 to 0.8 marked as deprecated. Each one now fails at startup with a message that names what to use instead and links here, so an upgrade can't quietly change how your chat behaves. After 1.0, ChatCops follows semver strictly: a breaking change waits for 2.0.

Go through the sections for the packages you use. If you're on 0.5 or earlier, read [Upgrading from 0.5](/getting-started/upgrading/) first.

Theming

ChatCops uses a theme engine that applies CSS custom properties to the Shadow DOM host element.

Installation > Core (Optional)

Only needed if building custom integrations:

```bash
npm install @chatcops/core
```

Provides direct access to providers, tools, knowledge base, and i18n:

```typescript
import { createProvider, LeadCaptureTool, FAQKnowledgeSource } from '@chatcops/core';
```

Installation

ChatCops consists of three packages. Install only what you need.

ChatCopsBot

If you saw `ChatCopsBot` in your server logs, a site is building a search index for its ChatCops chat assistant with [`@chatcops/ingest`](/core/knowledge-base/#building-an-index-from-your-site). ChatCops is open source software that each site runs itself, so the requests come from whoever is running it, not from a central ChatCops service. Usually that's you, or someone indexing a site they look after.

The user agent looks like this:

```
ChatCopsBot/0.1 (+https://chat.codercops.com/bot)
```

Widget Configuration

The widget can be configured via `data-*` attributes on the script tag or programmatically via `ChatCops.init()`.

Analytics > Tracked Events

When `analytics: true`, the server automatically tracks:

| Event | When |
|-------|------|
| `conversation.started` | New conversation ID first seen |
| `message.sent` | User sends a message |
| `message.received` | AI responds |
| `lead.captured` | Lead capture tool fires |

`ANALYTICS_EVENTS` from `@chatcops/core` has these names, so code doesn't have to spell them. Before 0.8 they were `conversation:started`, `message:sent`, `message:received` and `lead:captured`. Stats still count events a store saved under those names, so totals carry on across the upgrade, but `track()` and `getEvents()` treat them as names of your own. Webhook event names, such as `lead:captured` in a webhook's `events`, are separate and didn't change.

AI Providers > Default models

| Provider | Default model | SDK | Streaming |
|----------|---------------|-----|-----------|
| Claude | `claude-haiku-5-5` | `@anthropic-ai/sdk` | `messages.stream()` |
| OpenAI | `gpt-5-mini` | `openai` | `chat.completions.create({ stream: true })` |
| Gemini | `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` | `@google/genai` | `models.generateContentStream()` |

Set `model` to use any other model the provider offers.

Cloudflare Workers Adapter > Notes

- Cloudflare Workers have a 30-second CPU time limit (Bundled plan) or 15 minutes (Unbound)
- SSE streaming works natively on Workers
- Use Cloudflare KV or D1 for persistent storage (conversation history, analytics)
- The `env` object provides access to secrets and bindings
